name: West Virginia

notes: Food and food ingredients, candy and soft drinks included, are exempt from the state and municipal sales taxes; prepared food is taxed at 6% plus the municipal 1%. The soft drink excise tax ended June 30, 2024.

Alcohol is taxed at the sales tax rate. Liquor and wine bought in stores also pay a 5% tax for cities and counties, which isn't counted here (it falls on only liquor and wine, not beer, and no official figure gives their share of alcohol bought in stores), nor are wine's 26.4 cents a liter or beer's $5.50 a barrel. Drinks served in bars, restaurants and clubs pay the ordinary sales tax (plus any city sales tax), counted for drinks served; the 5% taxes aren't collected on their sales (clubs pay them, and the sales tax, when they buy liquor and wine).

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the sales tax rate, on top of excise taxes left out here: $1.20 a pack of 20 cigarettes, 12% of the wholesale price on other tobacco, and 7.5 cents a milliliter of e-cigarette liquid.
Household supplies: diapers are taxed, except during the August holiday, when they count as clothing; 2026 bills to exempt them didn't pass.
Personal care products: menstrual products are taxed in full; 2026 bills to exempt them didn't pass.
Barber and beauty services: barbering, hairstyling, manicuring and massage are personal services, which aren't taxed.

Clothing is taxed, except items of $125 or less during the yearly sales tax holiday (July 31 to August 3 in 2026; it also covers laptops and tablets up to $500, school supplies up to $50 and sports equipment up to $150), which is not taken out here.
Laundry and dry cleaning are taxed, coin-operated washers and dryers included.
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and pays 35.7 cents a gallon in 2026 instead, left out here.
The municipal 1% doesn't apply to motor vehicles (which pay a 5% DMV tax instead) or motor fuel.

Hotel stays pay the sales tax plus county or city hotel occupancy taxes (6% in most counties and larger cities; a county's applies only outside cities), and in the Snowshoe Resort Area District a 2% resort fee; not counted here.
The services below are from W. Va. Code 11-15-8 (all services are taxed except professional and personal services) and the Tax Division's guides.
gaps: West Virginia has no county sales taxes; 101 municipalities levy 1% (Tax Division list, October 2026), and Danville, Farmington, Gilbert, Kenova, Keyser and Wellsburg begin 1% on January 1, 2027 (named on their pages, not yet in the rates).

Six Economic Opportunity Development Districts (Huntington, Charles Pointe, University Town Centre, The Highlands, Park Place and The Ridges) collect a special district excise tax in place of the state sales tax at the same rate, so rates there are the same. Hotel stays also pay county or city hotel occupancy taxes (up to 6%), and the Snowshoe Resort Area District a 2% resort fee; not counted.
Food and drug items carry a different rate here (state 0%), and a different local rate where the locality sets one. What counts as food follows the state's rules.

as mapped in 2022; the city's 2025 ten-year report on TIF Project 1 shows the district in force

programs: Tax increment financing districts are mapped for Morgantown (five districts) and Fairmont (one, active in the city's 2025 report). Not mapped: Elkins' TIF district, Wheeling's downtown TIF district, Berkeley County's North and South TIF districts, Harrison County's and Monongalia County's (University Town Centre) TIF districts, and Charleston's City Center business improvement district. Main Street West Virginia and ON TRAC publish no current list of their communities (11 accredited Main Street and 14 ON TRAC communities in February 2024).

Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.
